answer: Resist Sybils with prediction-accuracy standing: each identity must lock in forecasts of verifiable public events before they happen, and only accurate forecasts build standing over many epochs, like a cipher that reveals itself one clue at a time. An echo of one good prediction earns nothing: forecasts are salted per identity, so clones cannot copy a single answer, and a wharf of fake accounts must each make its own bets, paying the cost of being wrong again and again. A pattern of careless guesses exposes fakery, while honest agents accumulate a record no farmer can fabricate cheaply.
